newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Metway says current year looking good.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Metway says current year looking good.

text.p: Metway Bank Ltd's outlook for 1996/97 is looking good with business volume levels looking up, new chief executive Greg Moynihan told a news conference.
"The current year is looking quite good, and volume levels are looking up," Moynihan said. "Overall asset growth for 1996/97 will be stronger than last year," he added.

"We can expect, while there is margin pressure, volumes are starting to pick up in both housing and business areas," he said. "Particularly in business markets for 96/97, we can expect them to be very buoyant," he said.
Moynihan, speaking after the release of 1995/96 results, said costs would be cut further in 1996/97.
"On the cost side of things, we've been able to bring our cost ratios down quite vigourously," he said.
"Despite the margin pressures, we are very well placed to withstand those," he said.
Metway earlier announced at net profit of A$41.69 million for the year to June 30, down from A$50.39 million a year earlier.
Competion during the 1995/96 year "was as fierce as anything we've seen, but we've held our own," Moynihan said.
He said recent cuts in mortgage interest rates had started to stimulate demand.
"Our level of lending has started to pick up," he said.

Chairman Frank Haly told the news conference the due diligence process for the proposal to merge Metway with state government-owned entities Queensland Industry Development Corp and Suncorp Insurance and Finance was proceeding well with the end of October scheduled for shareholder approval meetings.
